key_fields.sql: select payment_type, count(*) as trips from lake.trips group by payment_type order by payment_type

value.bottleneck: The query performs a full sequential scan of 495,833 rows from the trips table followed by a hash aggregation on payment_type. The scan dominates execution time since every row must be read and processed despite only 5 distinct groups in the result.

hypotheses.claim: The SEQ_SCAN reads all columns or incurs decompression overhead for payment_type; a columnar projection pushdown or predicate pushdown (if filterable) could reduce I/O and CPU.
The PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY builds a hash table for only 5 groups but still processes 495,833 rows individually; a pre-aggregated metadata cache or materialized view would avoid the scan entirely.
Multiple PROJECTION nodes compress/decompress payment_type between operators, adding per-row CPU overhead; fusing projections or using a more direct encoding path could reduce per-row cost.
